shared_elements: worked stone surface bearing carved decoration
framing/border bands enclosing the figured field
a row or band of repeated small rectangular units
rectilinear panel or box-like geometric motif
small enclosed square panels containing a sign-like motif
curved, possibly zoomorphic outline in the central field
justification: The clearest correspondence is structural rather than iconographic: both surfaces organise their imagery inside framing bands and include a band of repeated rectangular units (the hatched register on A, the grid strip along B's lower edge), plus small square fields holding a compact motif. Against that, the manner of execution is entirely different — A is bold three-dimensional relief with unmistakable animals (birds, quadrupeds, snake-like forms) stacked in registers, while B is a thin, uniform incised line drawing on a fan-shaped slab whose central subject is a single ambiguous curved object, so neither the subject matter nor the compositional order really matches.
